title: A skip link or landmarks let you go past the navigation bar
note: The first Tab did not expose a usable skip link in this run. Chromium’s accessibility tree exposed a main landmark after the header. NVDA announced the main landmark during landmark navigation.

title: All navigation bar items work with the keyboard
note: The header brand and Catalog, Registration and Student Profile navigation items were keyboard reachable. Enter opened the corresponding views.

title: Search and all filters work with the keyboard
note: Typing “computer” worked in #catalog-search. Arrow Down changed 6 dropdowns, including #filter-dept.

title: You can fill in and submit the registration form with the keyboard
note: Tab, arrow keys and Space as applicable let me complete #course-registration-form. Enter opened #confirmation-modal.

title: Course card buttons and table buttons (register / drop) work with the keyboard
note: Enter activated the catalog “Details” action and the Registration table “Drop” action.

title: The focus does not get stuck anywhere on the page
note: Forward and reverse Tab reached controls before and after the catalog filters, registration fields and course tables. Dialog confinement was checked under M2.

title: The focus order follows the visual order
note: At 1280 px, tabbing followed the header, then the visible controls in the Catalog, Registration and Student Profile reading order.

title: The focus is always visible
note: The focus indicator for “✔ Enrolled” in Catalog disappeared behind the sticky header during keyboard navigation.

title: The focused element is not hidden behind other content
note: The sticky header covered part or all of the focused “✔ Enrolled” control in Catalog during keyboard navigation.

title: The focus goes into the modal when it opens
note: Opening #confirmation-modal left focus on “Submit Registration” behind the overlay.

title: Tab and Shift+Tab stay in the modal while it is open
note: Tab and Shift+Tab escaped #confirmation-modal, reaching the background control #btn-clear-selection.

title: Esc and the close or cancel button close the modal
note: Escape and the Close control dismissed #course-details-modal.

title: The focus goes back to the button that opened the modal
note: After using Close in #course-details-modal, the original Details button did not regain focus.

title: VoiceOver says that a dialog opened and reads its name
note: #confirmation-modal has role="dialog", aria-modal="true" and an aria-labelledby title reference. NVDA gave no dialog announcement when the overlay opened.

title: Each field has a visible label and VoiceOver reads it
note: Visible Registration labels are associated with their fields in #course-registration-form, including #reg-course-select. NVDA spoke “Grading Option star” on #reg-grade-option.

title: Required fields are marked with text or a symbol that is explained (not color only)
note: #reg-course-select is required in Registration. The form lacks an explanation for the required-field markings.

title: An empty or wrong submit shows each error in text next to its field
note: #toast-container briefly said “Please choose a course from the dropdown first.” No inline error appeared beside #reg-course-select.

title: Each error message tells how to correct it
note: The corrective instruction was available only in the temporary toast after submit.

title: VoiceOver reads the errors after submit
note: NVDA announced “Please choose a course from the dropdown first” via the toast. Focus stayed on #btn-submit-registration, so this failed the rubric’s focus-transfer requirement.

title: VoiceOver reads the result count after a search or filter change and the focus stays in place
note: #catalog-counter-text changed after “computer” was entered. The new count was outside a live region, and no separate live region received it. NVDA gave no result-count announcement during typing or the filter change.

title: VoiceOver reads the confirmation after you register or drop a course
note: NVDA gave no spoken add confirmation when Registration Success opened. It announced the course-specific drop message.

title: Each page or view has a title that tells what it is
note: Home, Catalog, Registration and Student Profile all retained the title “Apex University - Course Registration Portal”. NVDA’s title command read the Catalog title as “Apex University - Course Registration Portal”.

title: Headings: one h1 per view and levels in a logical order
note: Catalog jumps from “Course Catalog” (h1) to the course-title h3 elements. NVDA read the sampled catalog heading levels in browse mode.

title: Landmarks: banner or header and navigation and main and footer
note: Chromium exposed banner, main navigation, main content and contentinfo landmarks in each view. NVDA landmark navigation announced navigation, main, content info.

title: Link and button names tell what they do
note: Multiple Catalog card controls expose only “Details” or “Register” as their accessible name. NVDA read both sampled controls as “Details, button”.

title: Meaningful images and icons have a text alternative and decorative ones are hidden
note: The decorative header SVG inside .brand-icon-wrapper has no aria-hidden attribute and is exposed as an unnamed image. NVDA’s graphic shortcut from the top of Catalog found no announced graphic.

title: VoiceOver reads the column header for each cell of the registered-courses table
note: The registered-courses table uses th elements for “COURSE CODE” and other columns, but omits scope="col". NVDA announced column information while moving across the sampled registered-courses table cells.

title: Dropdowns and toggles and tabs announce their role and state (for example expanded or selected)
note: NVDA spoke the #mobile-menu-toggle button label without an expanded or collapsed state. The catalog dropdown exposed its combo box role and selected value.

title: The navigation bar tells which page is the current page
note: Activating a header item changed its active class only. The current link or button had no aria-current="page".

title: At 320 px width there is no horizontal scroll and no content is lost
note: At 320 × 568 px, the registration form and schedule layout extended past the page edge. In Registration, the document measured 969 px wide in a 305 px content viewport.

title: At 200% zoom all text is readable and nothing is cut off or on top of other content
note: At actual 200% Chrome zoom, Registration reached 969 px across a 632 px content viewport and displayed a page-level horizontal scrollbar.

title: Errors and status and selected filters are not shown by color only
note: The active Catalog and Registration links change foreground and background styling without a persistent text or icon cue. Course availability badges do include text.

title: Focus indicators and field borders have a contrast of at least 3:1
note: The #filter-dept field border (#e2e8f0) measured 1.23:1 against #ffffff, below 3:1.

title: The needs-review contrast sample passes (4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text)
note: The Registration “Part-Time Status” label measured 2.05:1 (#f59e0b on #f8fafc), below 4.5:1.
